rework: Attempt 2 addresses the orchestrator's script-only rework request. (1) `scripts/publish-release.sh` now pushes the existing branch and tag before publishing the GitHub release when run in `--release-only` mode (and only there): it first verifies the derived `--tag` exists locally and exits 1 with a clear message if not, then, unless `--no-push` was passed, runs `git push origin "$branch"` and `git push origin "$tag"` before creating/refreshing the release; the header comment and `usage` help text document this. All other behaviour is unchanged.

known_limitations: The release-only push itself (`git push origin <branch>` / `git push origin <tag>`) was not executed because the task forbids pushing; only the tag-existence gate and the `--no-push` skip branch were exercised, plus code inspection. The actual remote push and the subsequent gh/REST release create/upload/verify paths remain unexercised end-to-end.

The --prepare-only and --release-only modes were not fully executed because the task forbids committing, tagging, pushing, and calling GitHub; they are validated by `bash -n`, by the dry run exercising the shared metadata/checksum/manifest code path, by the two release-only gate tests above, and by code inspection.
The environment has neither the gh CLI nor GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN, so a real GitHub release was neither performed nor possible here; the release path exits 1 with the manual-step message.

manifest.json's `timestamp` is generated from the current UTC time at run time, so repeated release runs (different timestamps) intentionally differ; byte-identical output is guaranteed only for identical inputs, which was verified with a fixed timestamp. The committed manifest.json carries the re-run dry-run timestamp and will be regenerated/committed by task 8.6.
The build.yaml parser intentionally supports only the documented shape (quoted `key: "value"` scalars and folded `>` blocks for description/changelog); it does not implement general YAML.
The GitHub REST fallback requires `jq` (checked and errored clearly if absent); the gh branch and the manifest checksum extraction do not require jq (the latter falls back to sed).
The script derives the tag by stripping one trailing `.0` from the build.yaml version, per the task; versions not ending in `.0` keep their full dotted form with a `v` prefix.
